latest_apis.rationale: Fully on the current stable release and uses only current-generation APIs, but the router's Link primitive is used only for the header nav — card, pagination, move, type and evolution links are plain anchors, so the app is effectively MPA and forgoes Qwik City's client-side navigation and prefetching.

platform.rationale: Reaches for the platform first everywhere: fetch/undici, URLSearchParams, Map/Set, native form semantics, token-driven CSS; zero polyfills or hand-rolled replacements. Only nits: API URLs are built by string concatenation rather than new URL(), and fetches carry no AbortSignal.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts — all PokeAPI access, caching and id mapping live in one module with a promise-level in-memory cache (api.ts:10-30) that evicts misses/failures
app/src/lib/api.ts:6-8 — API_BASE_URL resolved once at module load; the only configuration point

app/src/adapters/node-server/vite.config.ts:13-16, app/src/entry.node-server.tsx:13-17 — adapter and server entry mirror the official generator output, so regenerating them would produce a near-empty diff
app/src/lib/api.ts:13 — apiGet returns Promise<any>; loaders rely on any-typed fields (routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:48-140), so API shape changes surface as runtime bugs
app/src/lib/api.ts:86 vs app/src/routes/types/[name]/index.tsx:24 — EXCLUDED_TYPES defined twice
app/package.json:6-13 — typescript installed but no 'typecheck'/'lint' script, and eslint-plugin-qwik (which catches resumability regressions) is absent
churn_resistance.rationale: Excellent structural isolation (one API module, one pure-helpers module, generator-faithful adapters, no framework internals or undocumented behavior), so a Qwik upgrade would touch few files; the deductions are the any-typed API boundary, one duplicated constant, and missing static-check tooling.

findings.issue: Almost all internal links are plain <a> (cards, pagination, move/type links, abilities, evolution, type lists); Qwik City's Link is used only in the header and not-found page. Plain anchors cause full page reloads instead of client-side SPA navigation and lose Qwik City's link prefetching (verified against Qwik docs/tutorials).
findings.suggestion: Replace internal <a> with Link from '@builder.io/qwik-city' so the router performs client-side navigation and prefetches routes.

findings.issue: Every PokeAPI response is typed any, and route loaders lean on any-typed fields (e.g. app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:48-140, routes/moves/[name]/index.tsx:13-33). A change in the API's shape becomes a runtime bug on a page rather than a compile error, despite strict mode being on (app/tsconfig.json:12).
findings.suggestion: Define response interfaces (species, pokemon, move, ability, type, generation, version-group) alongside the app DTOs in lib/api.ts so the boundary between raw API data and app state is checked by the compiler.

findings.issue: EXCLUDED_TYPES ('stellar', 'unknown', 'shadow') is duplicated in api.ts and in routes/types/[name]/index.tsx:24.
findings.suggestion: Export it once from lib/api.ts and import it in the route.

findings.issue: API fetches have no timeout/abort; a stalled upstream request also stalls the in-flight promise that is cached for its lifetime.
findings.suggestion: Pass AbortSignal.timeout(...) to fetch, or fall back to a fresh fetch on rejection so one hung request cannot block the cached promise forever (rejection eviction already exists at api.ts:31-34; a hang does not reject).

findings.issue: typescript is installed but no script runs it ('typecheck'/'tsc --noEmit' absent), and eslint-plugin-qwik — which the official starters ship to catch resumability pitfalls — is not included.
findings.suggestion: Add a typecheck script and eslint-plugin-qwik as devDependencies so regressions are caught statically before they ship.

findings.issue: build.server drops the 'qwik check-client src dist' guard that the official 1.20.3 node-server adapter's generated script includes.
findings.suggestion: Match the generated script ('qwik check-client src dist && vite build -c adapters/node-server/vite.config.ts') so a stale client build fails the build instead of deploying.

findings.issue: typescript is declared with a stale floor '^5.6.0' (the lockfile resolves the current 5.9.3).
findings.suggestion: Raise the declared floor to the version actually used, so a future lockfile regeneration doesn't silently allow an older toolchain.

summary: This is a genuinely current Qwik app: both framework packages are pinned to the latest stable release (1.20.3, five days old) and the adapter/server entry mirror the official generator output almost exactly, so a Qwik upgrade would touch very few files. All data access is isolated behind one well-designed module, dependencies are as lean as the framework allows, and platform usage is exemplary. The two things I'd ask the author to fix before merging are switching internal links to Qwik City's Link (the app currently pays full page reloads on every card click) and typing the PokeAPI responses instead of using any throughout the loaders.
